# Takeout Photo

> Takeout Photo is a desktop app for Mac and Windows that runs on your own computer and reads your Google Takeout export in place (.zip and .tgz archives, without unpacking them). It turns your Google Photos into a private timeline of trips, places and maps, matches your photos to your Strava, Komoot or Garmin Connect activities along the GPS track, or moves them to Proton Photos with albums and metadata intact. A Docker image for a NAS (beta) runs it on your home network. Everything is processed locally; your photos are never uploaded to our servers.

## Download

- [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg): the latest release as a .dmg. Apple silicon (arm64) only, macOS 12 (Monterey) or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized. The app updates itself (Sparkle; "Check for Updates…" menu, automatic checks can be turned off in Settings → Updates). [Release notes](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases).
- [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe): the latest release as an installer (.exe); a portable [TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64.zip](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64.zip) is also available. Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The Windows app isn't code-signed yet, so the first launch shows "Windows protected your PC" — click "More info", then "Run anyway". It doesn't update itself automatically yet (coming soon); new versions are on the [releases page](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases).
- Free to download and explore: the sample library in the app or the [read-only demo](https://takepho.com/demo/). Importing your own Takeout needs a plan (see Pricing).
- Self-host on a NAS (beta): run the Docker image with Docker Compose on your home server or NAS and open it in the browser on your network. See [Self-hosting](https://takepho.com/self-host/).

## Self-hosting on a NAS (beta)

- Run the same app and the same three apps (Photos timeline, Activities, Proton Photos sync) on your NAS or home server with Docker Compose, in your browser on your network: [Run Takeout Photo on a NAS with Docker Compose](https://takepho.com/self-host/).
- Image: `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho:latest` (amd64 and arm64); optional CUDA image `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho-cuda:latest` for an NVIDIA GPU. `:latest` always points at the newest release; every release also has a pinned tag, e.g. `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho:1.0.0` and `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho-cuda:1.0.0`. Requires Docker Engine with Compose v2.24+, an x86-64 or 64-bit ARM CPU and 4 GB RAM free for the container (8 GB recommended for big libraries).
- Same plans and prices as the desktop app (see Pricing); the NAS counts as one of your account's 2 computers, and it needs internet at least once a month to refresh the licence.
- Security: the app has no login of its own; keep it on your home network or behind a VPN or an authenticated reverse proxy, and never forward the port to the internet.

## How it works

1. Request your Takeout at [takeout.google.com](https://takeout.google.com): your export arrives as one or more archive files (takeout-001.zip, ...).
2. Takeout Photo processes it on your computer: it reads .zip/.tgz archives in place without unpacking, from a folder, a Google Drive link, or read-only Google sign-in; it reads the JSON sidecars for the real dates, GPS and descriptions; it handles libraries of hundreds of GB; newer exports merge in (incrementally on the yearly plan, rebuild with edits kept on Lifetime). Your photos are never uploaded.
3. Open your apps: the Photos timeline, Activities (photos on Strava, Komoot and Garmin Connect activities), Proton Photos sync. Each app appears for the data your export contains.

## Pricing

- **Lifetime licence**: one-time USD 25. Import your Takeout manually; importing a newer export rebuilds the library with your edits (hidden photos, trip names/notes, homes, people) kept; all app updates included.
- **Yearly subscription**: USD 25 for the first year, then every renewal is automatically 50% off (USD 12.50 per year). Everything in Lifetime plus automatic processing (folder watcher imports new exports as they land, incremental imports of newer exports without rebuild, contributors such as a partner's Takeout). The first paid year includes the Lifetime licence: if you cancel, you keep it.
- Prices include taxes; the currency is picked from your country at checkout: USD 25 (United States and rest of the world), EUR 20 (Europe), GBP 20 (United Kingdom), CHF 20 (Switzerland and Liechtenstein) — these are the first-year prices, and yearly renewals after the first year are half price (USD 12.50, EUR 10, GBP 10, CHF 10).
- Buy inside the app: Settings → Account, sign in with Google or Apple, choose a plan and pay. Prices include taxes; cancel any time from the app's "Manage subscription" button. One account covers 2 computers. The app works offline on a signed entitlement, refreshed about weekly (internet at least once a month).

## What you can do with your Google Photos Takeout

- [Google Photos Takeout viewer: browse your export as a timeline](https://takepho.com/google-photos-takeout/): read the .zip/.tgz archives in place, get the real capture dates and GPS from the JSON sidecar files, and browse trips, places and routes on a map.
- [See your Google Photos on your Strava activities](https://takepho.com/google-photos-strava/): sync activities from Strava (official API, OAuth), Komoot or Garmin Connect (your own login) and match your Takeout photos to each activity by capture time, placed along the GPS track ("km 12.3 · 10:42").
- [Move your Google Photos to Proton Photos](https://takepho.com/google-photos-to-proton-photos/): import the Google Photos part of your Takeout into Proton Photos (Proton Drive) in full original quality, with albums or trip albums, and capture date, GPS, description, favourite and people written losslessly into the files from the Takeout JSON sidecars, uploaded via Proton's official open-source Drive CLI.
- Coming next: more sync destinations beyond Proton Photos, and support for Google Drive and Google Docs files from your Takeout (today only the Google Photos part is used).
- [Home](https://takepho.com/): download, how it works, apps, platforms, pricing, FAQ.
- [Read-only demo](https://takepho.com/demo/): try the app in your browser with a sample library.
- [Self-hosting on a NAS (beta)](https://takepho.com/self-host/): Docker Compose on your home server or NAS.

## Status

The Mac app (Apple silicon) and the Windows app (Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit) are downloadable now, see Download above. A Docker image for a NAS is in beta. A live read-only demo is at https://takepho.com/demo/.

## Privacy

Everything is processed locally on your computer; your photos are never uploaded to our servers. If you sign in with Google, access is read-only and limited to the files you pick. The account service (account.takepho.com, hosted on Hetzner in Germany) stores only your sign-in identity, your purchase records (no card data) and your registered devices (device id, name, last seen); it is backed up nightly (14 days). Full policy: https://takepho.com/privacy.html
